clue.text: High point after New Year's Day for one cleaning up

indicators.note: placed after means the hilltop word follows the date in the answer

parts.note: 1 January, written JAN I
a tor is a rocky hilltop, a high point on a moor

explanation.surface: Someone tidying up after the New Year celebrations, reaching a high point of the holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts TOR behind JAN I, January 1st with the one as a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitor is a caretaker whose job is cleaning and maintaining a building.

clue.text: Woman changing gender in France in short trousers

indicators.note: short tells us the word for trousers loses its final letter

parts.note: jeans are denim trousers

explanation.surface: A woman crossing the Channel and switching gender while wearing cut-off trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' takes the last letter off JEANS. The definition works because Jean is a woman's name in English but a man's name in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean is a female first name in Britain, yet the French Jean is male, so the name changes sex across the Channel.

clue.text: Description of rank cod and onion men prepared, tucked into by girl

indicators.note: tucked into by means the girl word goes inside the reworked letters
prepared, as a cook prepares food, means the letters of these words are reworked

parts.note: miss is a young unmarried woman, a girl

explanation.surface: A girl tucking into a meal of cod and onions that some men have cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' gives the rearranged letters NONCOMIONED, which 'tucked into by' opens up for the girl. 'Tucked into' suggests eating, but here it means inserting.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-commissioned describes an officer such as a sergeant or corporal, a military rank held without a commission.

clue.text: One with faith is tense on a job

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
a job is slang for a robbery, a heist

explanation.surface: A believer who is nervous about starting work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a job' is criminal slang for a robbery, and 'tense' is the grammar abbreviation, not nervousness.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist is someone who believes in a god, a person with religious belief.

clue.text: Character in Sophocles married sexually open-minded figures

parts.note: Sophocles wrote in Greek, and rho is a letter, a character, of the Greek alphabet
bi is short for bisexual

explanation.surface: A figure from a Greek tragedy who is married yet sexually liberal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' means a letter, not a role in a play: RHO is a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhombi are geometric shapes, plural of rhombus, a four-sided figure with equal sides.

clue.text: Nothing on course to relieve irritation

definitions.meaning: a golfer of this standard plays off a zero handicap on the golf course
to rub an itchy patch with the fingernails to ease it

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a zero golf handicap, and also the act of rubbing skin with nails to soothe an itch.

clue.text: Formally induct government that's promising

parts.note: to swear in an official is to install them by having them take an oath

explanation.surface: The swearing-in of a new government that looks full of promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Swearing means vowing or giving one's word, the same as making a promise.

clue.text: Dump large grass skirts, getting made over

indicators.note: skirts as a verb means goes around the edge of, so the grass word surrounds the others

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a sty is a filthy place, a dump
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Throwing out big grass skirts as part of a wardrobe makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirts' is a verb meaning goes round, not clothing, and 'Dump' is a noun for a squalid place, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Restyled means given a new look, as in a makeover of hair or clothes.

clue.text: Work set in France and Spain, then US and Israel's so awful

definitions.text: Work set in France and Spain

indicators.note: awful here means bad, mangled, so the letters of these words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A commentator lamenting how badly the US and Israel are behaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges THEN, US, ISRAELS and SO. The definition takes up the clue's first half.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemingway's 1926 novel follows expatriates from Paris to the bullfights of Pamplona in Spain.

clue.text: Leave time to get star into successful promo

indicators.note: into means the time and star pieces are placed inside the other two pieces

parts.note: a hit is a success, as in a hit show
a promo is a promotion, an ad
a star of a story is its hero

explanation.surface: An ad agency wanting the celebrity in its campaign before leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' splits 'successful promo' into its two words' synonyms and puts the time-plus-star piece between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit the road is an idiom for departing or setting off on a journey.

clue.text: Nurses undressed in Broadway show

indicators.note: undressed means stripped of the outer layer, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: nannies are children's nurses

explanation.surface: Nurses performing naked in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undressed' strips the outer letters from NANNIES. A nanny was once called a nurse in British households.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie is the 1977 Broadway musical about the orphan Little Orphan Annie.

clue.text: Poetry covering page in old books was extravagant

indicators.note: in means the poetry piece sits inside the old-books pair

parts.note: NT, New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

indicators.note: covering means the poetry word goes around the page letter

parts.note: verse means poetry

explanation.surface: Someone who spent too much on antiquarian poetry books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' gives VERSPE, and 'in' puts that between the old and books pieces; 'books' here are the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: To have overspent is to have paid out more than one could afford, which is extravagance.

clue.text: Third person by eighth vehicle? It may be fruitful

parts.note: to play gooseberry is to be the unwanted third person with a couple
a bus is a vehicle
H is the eighth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a third passenger seated beside the eighth vehicle in a line.
explanation.walkthrough: In British idiom, the 'gooseberry' is the third person tagging along with a couple. 'eighth' is the alphabet's eighth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A gooseberry bush bears fruit; British children were told babies come from under one, a further sense of fruitful.

clue.text: Good stuff! Work by Polish player from long ago

parts.note: to ram is to stuff or cram
op, from opus, is a musical work
to hone is to polish or sharpen

explanation.surface: Praise for a piece of music by a composer from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is the verb meaning refine, not the nationality, despite its capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone is an old-fashioned record player from the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Resistance with some current inclination

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance
an amp is a unit measuring electric current, so a measure of some current

explanation.surface: An electrical engineer's account of resistance, current and slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is a slope, and an inclination is a sloping surface or gradient.

clue.text: Peru and Iran unfortunately in run-down state

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of these names are scrambled

explanation.surface: Two countries, Peru and Iran, sadly in a dilapidated condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges PERU and IRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrepair is an old noun for disrepair, the condition of being neglected and dilapidated.

clue.text: In a jittery state, go as fire's spread

indicators.note: jittery means nervously shaking, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: fire's is read as fire is; only the letters of fire join the mix

explanation.surface: A nervous person urged to leave as a fire spreads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a jittery state' rearranges GO, AS and FIRE. 'spread' looks like a verb for the fire but is a noun for something spread on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Foie gras is a rich pâté of fattened duck or goose liver, often served smeared on toast.

clue.text: Monkey sports with one female between two rivers

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school sports

indicators.note: between means the one and female pieces sit inside the pair of rivers

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river, so two rivers give two Rs
I is the Roman numeral one
she is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: A monkey performing gymnastics alongside a female, between two rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' puts I and SHE inside R and R. Perisher is British slang for a cheeky child, and monkey is a common term for a mischievous child.
explanation.definitionFit: A perisher is a little rascal, just as a naughty child is called a little monkey.

clue.text: Firm is no merchant holding dubious label

indicators.note: holding means the answer is contained within these consecutive clue words

explanation.surface: A firm that is not a merchant holding a misleading brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' points to the letters inside 'firM IS NO MERchant'.
explanation.definitionFit: A misnomer is a wrong or inaccurate name, so a name that is questionable.

clue.text: Scottish island hiding unknown girl

indicators.note: hiding means keeping out of sight, so the unknown letter is removed

parts.note: Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides, famous for whisky
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A Scottish island concealing a mysterious young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' removes Y from ISLAY; algebra's unknowns are x, y and z. 'hiding' looks like a hidden-word signal but is a deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Isla is a female first name, popular in Scotland.

clue.text: Spot one like Rees-Mogg occupying grandiose residence

indicators.note: occupying means taking up residence inside, so the politician goes inside the residence word

parts.note: a pile is a large stately house
Jacob Rees-Mogg was a British Conservative Member of Parliament, an MP

explanation.surface: Seeing an aristocratic politician living in a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupying' places the politician after the first two letters of the house. Rees-Mogg, famous for his old-fashioned manner, lives in a grand country house.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimple is a small inflamed spot on the skin.

clue.text: Return of Pétain and Quisling, say, wanting power increase

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so one letter is taken out
return means turning back, so the word for these figures is read backwards

parts.note: Pétain in France and Quisling in Norway led puppet governments under Nazi Germany

explanation.surface: A historian discussing the return of wartime collaborators hungry for power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return of' reverses PUPPETS to STEPPUP, and 'wanting' removes one P.
explanation.definitionFit: To step up is to raise or intensify, as in stepping up production.

clue.text: May Eden, say, tend to be found between 11 and 13?

indicators.note: to be found between means the tend word sits inside the numbers word

parts.note: eleven and thirteen are both prime numbers, so primes
to minister is to tend or care for

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about where Theresa May and Anthony Eden appear among the clue numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May and Anthony Eden were both British prime ministers. '11 and 13' look like cross-references to other clues but are just prime numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: May and Eden are examples of heads of the British government.

clue.text: Piano tune for possible performers of duet

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A piano piece composed for two players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' just joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A duet needs two musicians, a pair, to perform it.

clue.text: Possession of unopened tranquillisers and joint

indicators.note: unopened means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: downers are slang for sedative drugs
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: Being found with unopened sedatives and a cannabis joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' removes the D from DOWNERS. 'joint' suggests cannabis but means the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Ownership is the state of owning something, its possession.

clue.text: Something on the menu is finished article

parts.note: past means over, finished
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A dish that is off the menu because it has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' just joins the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is a dish commonly listed on a restaurant menu.

clue.text: A lot of rudeness shocked consumer, finally

indicators.note: shocked means violently disturbed, so the remaining letters are jumbled
a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A customer finally appalled by staff rudeness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' drops the last S of RUDENESS, and 'shocked' rearranges RUDENES. 'finally' looks like a last-letter signal but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An end user is the person who ultimately uses a product, the last buyer in the chain.

clue.text: Retired model is a source of revelations

parts.note: ex means former, retired
a model is someone who poses, a poser

explanation.surface: A former fashion model telling all about the industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' just links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposer is someone who exposes, bringing secrets into the open.
